tasks.short: Write the monthly finance note for the three sites

today.trigger: The month is ready to close in AFAS, or a site lead asks why the margin moved.
steps: Export the trial balance and the site profit and loss from AFAS Profit.
Refresh Power BI and check it still matches that trial balance.
Collect late payroll journals and the three staffing-agency accruals.
Write a short note on margin, labour and cash for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Send it to the Finance Director and answer the questions that come back.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same site bridge in Excel every month.
Chasing agency invoices and payroll journals that are not in the ledger yet.
Rewriting the note after a late journal changes the figures.
today.time_sinks: Most of the five hours a month goes on tying Power BI back to AFAS and rewriting the note once late agency and payroll entries land.

lenses.faster: Building the site bridge and drafting the note disappear. Checking the tie-out and correcting the cause still takes about two hours of the five this note takes today.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS load starts it once the payroll journal and the agency accrual are in. The bridge and the draft note run on their own. The accountant releases the note before any site lead sees it.
lenses.ambitious: A one-page labour bridge for each warehouse manager, collective-agreement staff against flex, is a new note for people who today see only a company total. They would ask for it more often if it were cheap, because the flex pool swings from 150 to 300 people and that cost is what they argue about in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the Excel bridge. The work they want is explaining a real margin move to a site lead who can act on it.
lenses.options: One draft that puts the margin move on volume, one on the flex rate, and one on a late accrual, changes whether the Finance Director asks a site for a recovery plan this month or waits for the next close.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from assembling the pack to deciding which movements are solid enough to send. They gain the right to issue the monthly note without the controller rewriting it, and the job becomes more expert because the remaining work is the cause.
reach: The FP&A analyst's first-pass commentary on actuals, once the accountant can show the bridge from AFAS into the forecast categories.
The controller's routine assembly of the monthly pack, leaving the controller the call on what the business is told.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant can tell a roster change from a lost customer or a late credit note, and has to stand behind that cause when a warehouse manager disputes the note.
tasks.pattern_why: The site bridge follows fixed rules from AFAS. One model call turns that bridge and the late-item list into a short note the accountant can check. The path is the same every month, so an agent is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS locks the period, after the payroll journal and the staffing-agency accrual are posted.
steps: A scheduled job builds the site bridge from the AFAS trial balance and stops if it does not tie to the ledger.
One model call drafts the note from the bridge, the open late items and last month's note.
The accountant corrects the causes and drops any line that is not tied out.
The accountant releases the note to the Finance Director and the site leads.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant releases each monthly note. The Finance Director receives only the released version.
data_needed: AFAS trial balance by site and cost centre
Payroll journal totals, without employee-level wage lines
Staffing-agency accrual by site
Prior month's note and the open late-item list
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close folder, with the tie-out file and the exact version the accountant released.

evidence.claim: Across 79 small and mid-sized firms, accountants using AI closed 7.5 days faster. That is a close-process result, not a measured saving on a Dutch logistics management note.
On four month-end scenarios, a model beat experienced accountants at detail, file search and following instructions. The same study left out client communication and asking the right questions.
On 160 US GAAP tasks the leading result meets 61.8% of criteria, 58% are never fully solved in eight attempts, and judgement is the bottleneck. This is not a Dutch GAAP test.
Once a ledger extract exists, a standard variance bridge can be built with rules. The model is needed for the wording, and the cause still has to be checked by the accountant.

risks: A draft that invents a cause for a margin move will reach site leads if the check only confirms that the totals tie.
Wage and flex detail is personal data under the AVG. The note should carry site totals.
If the note becomes a score of named planners or shift leads, the works council's consent for staff monitoring is in play.
research_questions: How many hours do the two accountants spend on the monthly note, and how much of that is rework after late agency invoices?
Do the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo warehouse managers act on a labour bridge, or do they only discuss cost when the Finance Director calls?
Over the last six closes, what share of margin movements had a cause that was not in AFAS, such as a verbal customer deal or a roster change?
Does the current Power BI model tie to the AFAS trial balance within a tolerance the controller already accepts?

tasks.short: Prepare the VAT return and the corporate tax return

today.trigger: A VAT period ends, or the corporate tax return comes due after the annual accounts are agreed.
steps: Map AFAS tax codes to the VAT return, including reverse charge and intra-EU transport.
Reconcile output VAT, input VAT and the ledger to the invoices the bookkeepers posted.
Roll the commercial result forward into the corporate tax computation.
Have the controller review the return and the amount to pay.
File and pay, then book the payment.
drudgery: Retyping AFAS tax totals into an Excel workpaper.
Hunting invoices on the wrong VAT code, especially agency invoices and foreign hauliers.
Copying last year's corporate tax bridge and updating each line by hand.
today.time_sinks: Of the 55 hours a year, the slow part is the VAT reconciliation on cross-border transport, warehousing for foreign principals, and staffing-agency invoices.

lenses.faster: Filling the VAT boxes from the tax codes and rolling the corporate tax bridge forward disappear. The reverse-charge, intra-EU and agency lines still take about three hours of the four and a half each period takes today.
lenses.autonomous: The AFAS period close starts the workpaper. The boxes fill from the tax codes, and Jonas runs its check where that AFAS function is switched on. Filing and payment wait for the accountant.
lenses.ambitious: A VAT treatment decided when commercial signs a new foreign-principal contract, rather than discovered at the next return, is a decision made far more often than today. Commercial managers in Rotterdam and Venlo would ask for it more often if it were cheap, because those contracts are how the sheds are filled.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying tax codes into Excel. They want the treatments that are genuinely uncertain.
lenses.options: One draft that treats a foreign principal's goods as warehousing, and one that treats the linked haul as an intra-EU supply, changes the VAT due and the price commercial should have charged.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes a review of exceptions and treatments. They keep the right to file, and they gain the right to send a treatment back to commercial before a contract is signed. The job is more expert.
reach: The controller's line-by-line check of a VAT return that already ties to AFAS, leaving the controller the uncertain treatments.
The FP&A analyst's tax line in the forecast, taken from the same bridge as the return.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to decide the reverse-charge treatment on cross-border transport and warehousing, and remains responsible for the filed return. AFAS states that the Jonas user keeps that responsibility.
tasks.pattern_why: The VAT boxes are a mapping from AFAS tax codes, and the corporate tax bridge is a roll-forward of differences that can be coded. Both run without a model. Jonas is a check on that draft, inside a workflow that is the same every period.

in_practice.trigger: The AFAS VAT period closes. Once a year, the approved commercial result is ready for the corporate tax return.
steps: AFAS fills the VAT return from the tax codes and lists invoices with no valid code.
Rules tie output VAT, input VAT and the reverse-charge boxes to the ledger.
Jonas checks the draft against the return and the help text, on AFAS versions that include it for the VAT return.
The accountant clears the exceptions, approves the payable, and files.
The corporate tax computation rolls forward from the last accepted bridge, and the accountant approves it before it enters the close.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves every VAT return and every corporate tax computation before filing or before the amount is posted. Correspondence with the Belastingdienst stays with a person.
data_needed: AFAS VAT codes and the general ledger
Invoice tax treatment, including intra-EU supplies and reverse charge
Last year's corporate tax bridge and the assessment
The commercial result after the statements are approved
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS tax dossier, with the Jonas check result and the accountant's approval stored on the return.

evidence.claim: From Profit 8, AFAS Jonas assists with corporate tax returns from 2022 and with the VAT return from 2026. It uses the return, the help centre and optional publisher content. The user remains responsible, and the data is not used for training.
Tax estimates belong on a mandatory human-review list. The computation can be prepared for approval.
No benchmark in the sourced material covers Dutch VAT. A tying return can still carry a wrong treatment.

The cabinet has chosen B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031. It is not law yet, and a PDF is not an e-invoice. Whether a 10-day deadline applies to domestic invoices is still open.

risks: A wrong tax code in AFAS produces a return that still ties to the ledger.
Jonas can propose a treatment the Belastingdienst would reject. The filing responsibility stays with the company.
Invoice lines can contain driver and agency-worker names. Keeping the work inside AFAS respects both the AVG and the AFAS rule that this data is not a training set.
Building a 10-day filing process now would follow a domestic deadline that is not settled.
research_questions: What share of VAT differences in the last four quarters came from reverse charge, intra-EU transport, and staffing-agency invoices?
Is the VAT return monthly or quarterly, and who files it in the Belastingdienst portal today?
Does the installed AFAS version include Jonas for the VAT return, and has a Jonas draft been compared with a return that was actually filed?
Over the last three years, how often did the corporate tax figure in the close differ from the figure on the filed return?

tasks.short: Review the balance sheet and the profit and loss

today.trigger: Month-end close, before the controller signs the figures.
steps: Tie bank, debtors, creditors, the payroll journal and fixed assets back to the AFAS ledger.
Scan material movements in assets, leases, provisions, revenue and labour cost.
Compare equity and the result with last month and with the budget in Power BI.
Send items that still look wrong back to the bookkeepers.
drudgery: Ticking subledgers off against the general ledger.
Rewriting flux comments that were already written last month.
Waiting on the Rabobank statement and the agency accrual before the review can start.
today.time_sinks: Of the 54 hours a year, reconciliations and the second pass after late entries take more time than the decision on whether a balance is right.

lenses.faster: The subledger tie-outs and the standard flux list disappear. Reading the material balances and sending back what is still wrong takes about two hours of the four and a half this review takes today.
lenses.autonomous: The AFAS close starts the tie-out once the bookkeepers mark the subledgers ready. Matches on bank, debtors, creditors, payroll and fixed assets run unattended. The review counts when the accountant signs it.
lenses.ambitious: A decision every month, while the flex pool is still on site, on whether the agency accrual is large enough for the season, is made far more often than today's wait for the invoice. The operations directors would want that figure on working day three if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking a subledger that already matches. They want the argument about a provision or a margin that changes the result.
lenses.options: One review that accrues the full agency estimate, and one that waits for the invoice, changes the month's result and what the sites think they earned.
lenses.altitude: The week is spent on breaks and on balances that move the result. They gain the right to hand the controller a review that already ties. The job is more expert.
reach: The bookkeeper's subledger reconciliation sign-off, once only the breaks are left.
The FP&A analyst's actuals-versus-budget check, which is rebuilt today from the same AFAS extract.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant can tell a missing accrual from a timing difference, and has to decide whether the result is solid enough for the controller to use.
tasks.pattern_why: The tie-out is a set of rules and needs no model. One model call then drafts the review of what moved, each point tied to a ledger line. The close follows the same path every month.

in_practice.trigger: The bookkeepers mark the subledgers ready and the Rabobank statement for the month is in.
steps: Rules tie the bank, debtors, creditors, the payroll journal and the fixed-asset register to the general ledger.
Lines inside the controller's tolerance drop out of the queue.
One model call drafts a review of the remaining movements, each with its ledger line.
The accountant accepts, corrects or returns each material item.
The signed review is the pack the controller uses for the close.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the review before the controller relies on it. The signed review is the close record.
data_needed: AFAS trial balance and the open subledgers
Rabobank CAMT.053 statement
Fixed-asset register
Payroll journal at total level
Agency accrual by site
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close binder for the AFAS period, with the exception list and the signed review.

evidence.claim: Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries and recommends schedules, and the teams stay responsible for review. Noordhaven would keep that split on an AFAS tie-out.
Models do well on month-end work that is file search and following instructions. Communication and tacit context were outside that test.
Judgement, not retrieval, is the bottleneck on accounting tasks, and multi-step reasoning is over half of the leading model's errors. A flux draft still needs a person.
A model that adds an assumption the workpaper cannot reproduce is a known failure. Every review point needs a ledger reference.

risks: A fluent explanation of a balance that does not cite the ledger line will survive a quick read and fail the auditor.
Lease terms and discount rates that sit in Excel will be missed if the review only reads AFAS.
The payroll tie-out must use journal totals. Employee-level wage lines are personal data and are not needed to review the result.
research_questions: Which subledgers fail to tie most often: bank, creditors, debtors, payroll, fixed assets, or the agency accrual?
What amount does the controller treat as small enough to roll into the next close?
How many review points in the last three closes were timing differences rather than errors?
Are the lease contracts and the fixed-asset register complete in AFAS, or do they still live in Excel?

tasks.short: Write the report of audit and control findings

today.trigger: The external auditor's interim or year-end visit, or an internal test that found a break.
steps: Collect exceptions from invoice samples, bank payments and journal-entry tests.
Write each finding with the amount, the cause and the ledger reference.
Draft the response with the bookkeeper or the payroll specialist who owns the booking.
Send the pack to the controller and the Finance Director before it goes to the auditor.
drudgery: Reformatting the same finding into the auditor's template.
Looking up the posting, the approver and the invoice for every sample item.
Chasing a written response from the person who made the booking.
today.time_sinks: Of the 54 hours a year, writing and rewriting the finding, and waiting for a colleague to confirm the cause, takes longer than spotting the break.

lenses.faster: Pulling the posting, the approver and the first draft of each finding disappears. Agreeing the cause and the response still takes about two and a half hours of the four and a half a typical finding cycle takes.
lenses.autonomous: A failed control test or an auditor request starts it. The draft finding, with amount and ledger link, is written on its own. It is issued only after the accountant and the control owner agree the response.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly decision with the Finance Director on whether a repeated break is fixed, instead of a promise made once a year in the management letter, is a decision made far more often than today. They would take that decision more often if the evidence were cheap, because open points are what become audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reformatting findings into a template. They want the conversation about which break is worth a new control.
lenses.options: One draft that calls a repeated IBAN change a control failure, and one that calls it a one-off, changes whether management promises the auditor a change in AFAS.
lenses.altitude: The week is about which findings matter and which response is true. They gain the right to put the internal findings log in front of the controller without a rewrite. Judging severity makes the job more expert.
reach: The controller's first draft of the response to the management letter.
The bookkeeper's collection of invoice copies for the auditor's sample, once AFAS produces the pack from the document link.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to judge severity, and whether the warehouse will actually carry out the response. The relationship with the external auditor stays with a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The tests that find the exceptions are rules. One model call turns an exception, and only those fields, into a finding in a fixed template. An agent is not needed to follow that template.

in_practice.trigger: A control test writes an exception, or the auditor opens a request on the year-end file.
steps: The exception log supplies the amount, account, user and AFAS document link.
One model call drafts the finding in the company template, using only those fields.
The accountant checks the draft against the source document.
The control owner agrees the response before the controller releases the pack to the auditor.
in_practice.human_gate: A finding leaves Finance only after the accountant has checked the source document and the control owner has agreed the response.
data_needed: Exception log with account, amount, user and document id
The source invoice, journal or payment
The finding template and last year's management letter
The user who approved the posting
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint audit folder for the financial year, with the source link and the version released to the auditor.

evidence.claim: Where the work is file search and following a template, models do well. A finding report is that kind of writing, and the study excluded the client conversation around it.
Multi-step reasoning across files is the main model failure. A finding that has to join an invoice, an approval and a policy still needs the accountant.
Products in this class prepare the accounting artefact and leave the review with the team.
No sourced benchmark covers a Dutch statutory audit file. The external auditor will re-perform the test from AFAS.

risks: A fluent finding that cites the wrong invoice will travel further than a rough note written by the accountant.
A write-up of who posted what becomes a personnel record if it is used to assess staff. The works council needs to be involved before that use.
The auditor re-performs the test. A finding that cannot be rebuilt from the AFAS document fails that re-performance.
research_questions: How many findings in the last two audits were missing documents rather than wrong amounts?
Does the auditor accept a SharePoint pack with AFAS document links, or do they still require a numbered PDF bundle?
Which control owners delay the response longest: the bookkeepers, payroll, or the site administrators?
Are IBAN changes and duplicate supplier invoices listed anywhere today, or only sampled when the auditor arrives?

tasks.short: Judge the company's VAT and corporate tax position

today.trigger: The close needs a tax figure, or a contract, an assessment or a Belastingdienst letter raises a new question.
steps: Start from the commercial result and list the differences that change corporate tax.
Review provisions, depreciation and the discount rate on long-term items such as leases.
Check VAT treatments that the standard tax codes do not settle.
Write the position and the amount to accrue, and walk the controller through it.
drudgery: Rolling the tax-difference list forward in Excel.
Re-reading lease contracts for the term and the rate.
Collecting last year's assessment, objections and letters.
today.time_sinks: Of the 50 hours a year, reading contracts and old tax letters, and rebuilding the bridge, takes longer than the final decision on the amount.

lenses.faster: Collecting the prior bridge, the assessment and the contract terms, and doing the arithmetic, disappears. Deciding which differences are defensible still takes about three hours of the four this position takes today.
lenses.autonomous: Close day two, a changed lease, or a Belastingdienst letter starts it. The bridge and a draft memo are prepared on their own. The amount is posted only after the accountant approves the estimate.
lenses.ambitious: A corporate tax position refreshed every month for the FP&A analysts, instead of once when the return is filed, is a decision made far more often than today. They would use it every forecast cycle if it were cheap, because the tax line now sits still until year-end.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss maintaining the Excel bridge. They want the position where the treatment could go either way.
lenses.options: One memo that accrues a VAT risk on foreign-principal warehousing, and one that treats it as unlikely, changes the tax line and what commercial is allowed to sign.
lenses.altitude: The week is positions and correspondence. They gain the right to put a numbered estimate into the close, which the controller can accept or challenge. The job is more expert because the routine arithmetic has left it.
reach: The controller's first formulation of an uncertain tax position in the annual accounts.
The FP&A analyst's tax accrual in the forecast, using the approved position.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to judge whether a position will survive the Belastingdienst, and carries the estimate. A model must not file it or send it.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic of a coded bridge can run as rules. The position itself starts from contracts and letters. One model call turns that file into a memo that lists the amount, the difference and every assumption, and the accountant accepts or rejects it.

in_practice.trigger: Close day two, or a new lease, a foreign-principal contract, or a Belastingdienst letter.
steps: Rules roll forward the last accepted tax bridge and calculate depreciation and discounting from rates the accountant has set.
One model call drafts the position memo from the bridge, the contract and the latest letter, and lists every assumption.
The accountant tests those assumptions against the contract and the prior assessment.
Only the approved amount is posted as the tax accrual.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves every tax estimate before it is posted. Letters to the Belastingdienst are sent by a person.
data_needed: Commercial result and the prior tax bridge
Lease contracts and the discount rate the accountant set
Depreciation and provision balances
Assessments and open objections
Written VAT treatments for foreign principals
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint tax file, with the assumption list and the approval stored next to the journal entry in AFAS.

evidence.claim: Tax estimates are on the mandatory human-review list. Preparation can be assisted. The decision to book the estimate stays with the company.
On broad accounting tasks, 58% are never fully solved in eight attempts and judgement is the bottleneck. A tax position is this kind of work, and the test set is US GAAP.
AFAS Jonas can assist on the corporate tax return, and the user remains responsible for the check. Assistance on the return is not a decision on an uncertain position.
A model that inserts an assumption the workpaper cannot reproduce leaves the accountant unable to defend the figure. The memo has to list assumptions separately from the arithmetic.

risks: An assumption buried in the prose will be posted if approval is a glance. The bridge has to be re-performable without the narrative.
A discount rate or a lease term that the draft fills in will misstate both the liability and the tax difference.
Dutch GAAP and Dutch VAT are outside the published benchmarks. A strong score on US tasks does not make this position reliable.
The file has to be one the Belastingdienst and the auditor can follow a year later.
research_questions: How large were the gaps between the tax accrual and the filed return over the last three years?
Are uncertain positions written down today, or do they sit in the accountant's mailbox?
Which inputs are outside AFAS: lease discount rates, foreign-principal contracts, open objections?
Will the external auditor rely on a memo whose arithmetic they can re-perform from the bridge?

tasks.short: Test the finance systems and recommend controls

today.trigger: The annual control plan, an auditor remark, or a payment that went to the wrong account.
steps: Review AFAS authorisations for who can create a supplier, change an IBAN and release a payment.
Sample journals, creditor invoices and Rabobank batches for segregation of duties.
See how staffing-agency invoices from the three portals enter the ledger.
Write the gap and a practical recommendation to the controller.
drudgery: Exporting user rights and comparing them by hand.
Sampling invoices that one rule could test in full.
Rewriting the same IBAN and duplicate-invoice recommendation each year.
today.time_sinks: Of the 49 hours a year, samples and rights exports take the hours. The recommendation is short once the evidence is on the table.

lenses.faster: Full-population tests replace the sample, so the export and the ticking disappear. Recommending a control and agreeing it with the controller takes about an hour and a half of the four hours this review takes today.
lenses.autonomous: Each posted invoice, journal and payment batch starts a test. Duplicates, segregation-of-duties breaks and IBAN changes are flagged on their own. A change to AFAS rights or to the payment process waits for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: A standing match of staffing-agency hours to the agency invoice, for site managers who have no internal time clerk for the flex pool, is a new service. They would use it every peak season if it were cheap, because that is when headcount moves between 150 and 300 and the invoices are hardest to check.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss sampling invoices that follow one rule. They want to design the control that stops the repeat finding.
lenses.options: A recommendation to hold any payment after an IBAN change until a second person approves, versus a recommendation to report the change after payment, changes whether the payment run slows down for the warehouses.
lenses.altitude: The week is spent on breaks that keep returning, and on which control is worth the friction. They gain the right to put a full-population exception log in front of the controller as evidence. The job is more expert because they write the test.
reach: The controller's upkeep of the AFAS authorisation matrix, once conflicts are listed every night.
The bookkeeper's duplicate-invoice check, which becomes a rule on the whole population.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to weigh a control against the speed of the warehouse payment run, and has to separate a fraud risk from seasonal noise. A rule will pass a collusion that follows the workflow.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicates, segregation of duties and IBAN changes are rules over AFAS and Rabobank data. They can run on every line with no model. The test list is fixed, so an agent adds nothing.

in_practice.trigger: Each night, after the AFAS posting run and the Rabobank statement import.
steps: Rules test every creditor invoice, journal and payment for duplicates, for a user who both changes a supplier and releases a payment, and for an IBAN change.
Breaks land in a queue with the document link.
The accountant reviews the queue and writes a recommendation where the same break keeps returning.
The controller approves any change to AFAS rights or to the payment process before it is switched on.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant clears the exception queue. No authorisation change and no change to the payment process is made until the controller approves it.
data_needed: AFAS user rights and the posting and approval user on each document
Supplier bank accounts and the date they changed
Invoice number, amount, supplier and date
Rabobank payment batches
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint exception log for the financial year, keyed to documents and roles, with no staff performance score.

evidence.claim: Judgement is where models fail, and multi-step reasoning is over half of the leading model's errors. Population tests of this kind should be rules, with the recommendation left to the accountant.
In the firm study, 62% of 277 accountants surveyed worry about AI errors. A flag is usable when it opens the AFAS document.
Duplicate invoices, segregation-of-duties conflicts and supplier bank-account changes can be expressed as queries over a ledger and a payment file.
Running payment files through a side model adds assumptions the test cannot reproduce. The test belongs in company systems.

risks: A log used to score employees, rather than to flag transactions, needs works council consent and can fall under the EU AI Act's employment rules.
Payment files contain names and account numbers. The tests should run in the company tenant.
The rules will flag genuine repeat agency invoices in peak season, and they will miss collusion that respects the approval path.
A rights change made in a hurry will stop a Rabobank payment run the warehouses are waiting on.
research_questions: How many duplicate payments and IBAN changes occurred in the last year, and how were they found?
Can AFAS export, for each document, the posting user, the approver and the supplier-bank change date?
Would the works council treat a nightly authorisation report as monitoring of staff?
What share of creditor invoices comes from the three agency portals, and do those invoices carry a stable invoice number?

tasks.short: Prepare and check the monthly and annual statements

today.trigger: Each month-end, and the year-end timetable for the annual accounts.
steps: Map the AFAS trial balance to the statement lines used last year.
Prepare the profit and loss, the balance sheet and the notes the board needs.
Verify the figures against the subledgers and the tax accrual.
Walk the controller and the Finance Director through the draft before the audit file is built.
Support filing of the annual accounts. For a large company that route is SBR, and AFAS does not file it.
drudgery: Copying the trial balance into the statement workbook.
Updating note wording where only the figure has changed.
Retieing the workbook to AFAS after every late journal.
today.time_sinks: Of the 49 hours a year, the statement workbook and the note roll-forward, including the second pass after late journals, take more time than the presentation decisions. The hours bunch at year-end.

lenses.faster: The mapping, the tie-out and the first draft of notes that only change by a figure disappear. Presentation, the tax note and the auditor's questions still take about half of the 49 hours, mostly at year-end.
lenses.autonomous: The period lock starts the monthly statements. The year-end calendar starts the draft annual accounts once the tax accrual is approved. The accountant signs the tie-out before either is issued.
lenses.ambitious: A decision at each close on the holiday-allowance and shift-premium accrual under the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, made with the payroll specialist, replaces a year-end true-up. The controller would want that decision every month if it were cheap, because those premiums move the result in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rolling last year's note wording forward. They want the presentation choices that change what the board and the auditor focus on.
lenses.options: Showing a warehouse lease in full as a long-term liability, or presenting the agency accrual inside accruals, changes ratios that Rabobank and the board both read.
lenses.altitude: The week is presentation, the notes that carry judgement, and the auditor's questions. They gain the right to hand the controller a statement that already ties to AFAS. The job is more expert.
reach: The controller's first draft of the annual accounts, leaving the controller the board conversation and the signing.
The FP&A analyst's actuals feed, taken from the same mapped statement.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to choose presentation under Dutch GAAP and Title 9 of Book 2 of the Civil Code, and has to defend it to the auditor. The draft is not the annual accounts.
tasks.pattern_why: Mapping the trial balance to statement lines is a rule, and the tie-out is the gate. One model call drafts the note wording from the tied-out figures and last year's text. Month-end and year-end follow a fixed route.

in_practice.trigger: The AFAS period lock for the monthly statements. For the annual accounts, the approved close and the approved tax accrual.
steps: Rules map the trial balance to the statement lines and stop if the mapping does not tie.
One model call drafts the notes that move with the figures, and marks every sentence that is new.
The accountant edits presentation, the tax note and anything the draft added.
The controller and the Finance Director review the year-end set before it goes to the auditor.
Filing with the KVK stays on the large-company SBR route. AFAS does not file that set.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the tie-out on every statement. The board and the auditor receive the signed version. Filing with the KVK is a separate step done by a person.
data_needed: AFAS trial balance
Statement mapping and last year's annual accounts
Approved tax accrual
Subledger tie-out
The prior KVK filing route and whether the company is large
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint statutory folder, with the mapping, the tie-out and the signed PDF kept for the auditor and the KVK file.

evidence.claim: The leading score on 160 US GAAP tasks meets 61.8% of criteria, and 58% are never fully solved in eight attempts. Dutch GAAP presentation is outside that test.
AFAS cannot file the annual accounts of a large company with the KVK. Large companies file through SBR from financial year 2025.
On detailed month-end scenarios, models handle file search and instructions well. Preparing statutory accounts also includes presentation choices that study left with the accountant.
Workday prepares accounting entries and revenue schedules and leaves review with the team. The same split fits a statement draft: the system prepares, the accountant signs the tie-out.

risks: Note wording that sounds finished will hide a mapping error if the tie-out is skipped.
Treating a high score on US GAAP benchmarks as evidence the Dutch annual accounts are right will produce audit adjustments.
If Noordhaven is large, a plan that has AFAS file with the KVK will miss the statutory deadline.
A cost-centre statement for a one-person department exposes that person's costs. Publish sites and functions.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven meet the large-company criteria, and who filed the last annual accounts with the KVK, through which SBR tool?
How much of the year-end Excel model is a straight map of AFAS, and how much is a manual adjustment a mapping would drop?
Which notes did the auditor change last year: tax, leases, provisions, or presentation?
Does the controller want a CAO labour accrual every month, or only a year-end true-up with the payroll specialist?

tasks.short: Check the bookings and talk to the people who made them

today.trigger: A close review, an audit sample, or a question on tax, CAO labour cost or an agency invoice.
steps: Pull the ledger lines, invoices and approvals for the area under review.
Compare them with the staffing portal, the warehouse receiving record or the Rabobank batch.
Interview the bookkeeper, the payroll specialist or the site administrator who made the booking.
Write down whether the recording is complete and which rule is still broken.
drudgery: Assembling the population before a useful question can be asked.
Interviewing people about bookings that were correct.
Writing up answers that all say the same thing.
today.time_sinks: Of the 44 hours a year, building the population and holding interviews on correct bookings takes more time than the few conversations that find a real gap.

lenses.faster: Assembling the population and setting aside the lines that match disappears. The interviews on the breaks still take about two and a half hours of the three and a half this check takes today.
lenses.autonomous: A close cycle or an audit sample starts the population match. The match against AFAS, the portal and the bank runs unattended. The conclusion waits until the accountant has spoken to the person who made the booking.
lenses.ambitious: A next-morning completeness check for night-shift supervisors in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo is a service for a group the accountants almost never meet, because interviews happen in office hours. Those supervisors would use an exception list more often if it were cheap and waiting at the start of their next shift.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss preparing a file of bookings that were already correct. They want the interview that explains a booking the ledger cannot.
lenses.options: Two explanations of the same break, a missed goods receipt or a delivery booked straight to cost, change whether the fix is a warehouse routine or a creditor accrual.
lenses.altitude: The week's conversations are only about breaks, including a call to a night-shift supervisor. They gain the right to close the areas the match cleared. The job stays expert because the interview and the compliance conclusion are the work.
reach: The bookkeeper's explanation of a creditor invoice that does not match a goods receipt, taken at the break.
The payroll specialist's confirmation that an agency accrual matches the approved hour total, at site level.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant can hear whether a booking was a workaround, a reading of the CAO, or a mistake, and can judge whether that explanation is credible. The interview stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: A match between a booking, a goods receipt, an agency hour total and a payment is a rule, and it can run across the whole population. The interview is the gate. The questions start only after the rule has listed the breaks.

in_practice.trigger: The close review or an audit sample selects creditors, agency cost, or goods receipts.
steps: Rules match AFAS lines to goods receipts, agency hour totals and Rabobank payments.
Matched lines are marked complete and left off the interview list.
The accountant interviews the bookkeeper, the payroll specialist or the site supervisor on the breaks.
The accountant writes whether the recording is complete and what must be re-booked.
in_practice.human_gate: A completeness conclusion is issued only after the accountant has spoken with the person responsible for the breaks, or has recorded why that conversation could not happen.
data_needed: AFAS journal lines with user and document id
Goods-receipt status held for finance
Agency hours and invoice totals by site, without worker dossiers
Rabobank payment references
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint compliance note for the period, with the population count, the break list and the interview note.

evidence.claim: The benchmark in which a model beat accountants left out asking the right questions and building tacit context. Those are the interview.
Multi-step reasoning across files is where models fail. The cross-check should be a rule, and the explanation should come from the person who booked it.
Matching a full population of bookings to goods receipts, hour totals and payments can be written as rules. The compliance conclusion depends on the interview.
Interview notes about identifiable workers are personal data under the AVG. The note should record the booking and the explanation.

risks: Pasting interview notes into an external model exports personal data. Keep the notes in SharePoint.
A clean match can hide a workaround the rule accepts. A new process still needs a conversation.
A night-shift check that feels like monitoring of warehouse staff needs a works council conversation before it starts.
If the three agency portals cannot export hours by site and week, the match cannot be built and the time saving disappears.
research_questions: What share of last year's interviews only confirmed a correct booking?
Can warehouse goods-receipt status be read from AFAS, or does it sit in a spreadsheet at the site?
Will night-shift supervisors take a call or a Teams note about a goods-receipt break at the start of the next shift?
Do the three agency portals export hours by site and week at a total that finance can store under the AVG?

role.altitude: The two accountants move from assembling packs and ticking entries to setting the tie-outs, the tax bridges and the tests that every entry has to pass. Their week becomes exceptions, tax positions and the conversations those create, and they gain the right to hand the controller a pack that already ties. The work becomes more expert. Days to close move only when the bookkeepers, payroll and the agency invoices keep up.
reach: The bookkeepers' subledger tie-out and duplicate-invoice chase, once only exceptions remain.
The controller's first draft of the monthly pack, the management-letter response and the notes to the annual accounts.
The FP&A analysts' actuals bridge and the tax line in the forecast, taken from the signed close.
The payroll specialist's reconciliation of the payroll journal to the ledger, at total level, leaving payslips and CAO interpretation with payroll.
role.ceiling_note: Two people cannot close faster than the bookkeepers, the payroll specialist and the three agency invoices allow. The board stays responsible for the annual accounts, the company stays responsible for the tax filing, and a person still speaks to the Belastingdienst and the external auditor. These eight tasks are about a quarter of the role. There is no Dutch GAAP or Dutch VAT benchmark, so review time stays. Works council consent limits any test that starts to look like monitoring of staff.
skills_to_grow: Writing tie-outs and test rules over AFAS, Rabobank CAMT.053 files and the agency exports, and reading the exceptions.
Dutch VAT on transport, warehousing and reverse charge, and the corporate tax bridge from the commercial result.
Title 9 presentation and the SBR filing path for a large company, outside AFAS.
The transport CAO and the warehouse CAO far enough to accrue holiday allowance and shift premiums with the payroll specialist.
When a finance test becomes personal data or staff monitoring, and when to involve the works council.
role.ambitious_version: The two accountants run a close the three sites can use by working day four: a flex-versus-CAO labour bridge for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo while the pool is between 150 and 300, a tax position commercial can read before signing a foreign-principal contract, and a control log the auditor can re-perform from AFAS. The hours that leave the Excel bridges go into those decisions, which are the ones that move days to close and audit adjustments.
